title: Securing Access to Storage

header.html: Configure Azure Storage firewalls and virtual networks; create and use shared access signature (SAS) tokens; configure stored access policies; manage access keys; configure identity-based access for Azure Files
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Firewalls and virtual networks

By default a storage account accepts requests from all networks. You can restrict access.

Setting Effect
Selected networks Allow only chosen virtual networks (subnets) and IP address ranges; everything else is denied
Service endpoint Lets a subnet reach storage over the Azure backbone; add the subnet to the storage firewall
Private endpoint Gives the account a private IP address in your VNet (through Private Link)
Trusted Azure services exception Allows certain Azure services (such as Backup) through the firewall
Disabled No public network access; use private endpoints only

Exam tip

. "Only VMs in one subnet may access the storage account" = storage firewall with a virtual network rule (service endpoint) or a private endpoint.

2Shared access signatures (SAS)

A SAS token is a signed URL query string that gives limited, time-bound access to storage without sharing the account key.

Type Signed with Notes
User delegation SAS Microsoft Entra credentials Most secure; Blob and Data Lake only
Service SAS The account key One service (blob, file, queue, table)
Account SAS The account key One or more services

A SAS defines permissions (read, write, delete, list), start and expiry time, optional allowed IP addresses, and HTTPS-only.

Exam tip

. A SAS signed with the account key stops working only when it expires, or when you rotate the key or delete the stored access policy it uses.

3Stored access policies

A stored access policy is defined on a container, share, queue or table and holds the SAS settings (permissions, start, expiry). A service SAS can reference the policy.

Benefit Detail
Revoke or change Edit or delete the policy to change or revoke all SAS tokens that use it, without regenerating account keys
Limit Up to five policies per container, share, queue or table

4Access keys

Each account has two access keys. A key gives full access to the whole account (shared key authorization), so protect it.

Practice Why
Two keys Rotate one while apps use the other
Store keys in Azure Key Vault Never in code
Prefer Entra ID and RBAC, or SAS Keys are all-powerful
Disallow shared key access Forces Entra ID authorization [Verify live]

5Identity-based access for Azure Files

Azure Files shares (SMB) can authenticate users with identities instead of the account key:

Identity source Use
On-premises Active Directory Domain Services Domain-joined clients
Microsoft Entra Domain Services Cloud-only or hybrid, managed domain
Microsoft Entra Kerberos Hybrid identities, without domain controllers in Azure [Verify live]

Access combines share-level permissions (Azure RBAC roles such as Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor) and NTFS file-level permissions. Blob data also supports Entra ID authorization with roles such as Storage Blob Data Contributor.

Exam tip

. "Users should sign in to the file share with their own domain identity" = identity-based access for Azure Files plus RBAC roles on the share.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A storage account must be reachable only from one subnet. What should be configured?

  • AA public container with a shared access signature that expires each week
  • BA storage firewall virtual network rule with a service endpoint
  • CA tag on the storage account that lists the allowed subnet
  • DA Read-only resource lock on the storage account
Show the answer

Answer: B. Network rules restrict access to chosen subnets.

S2A partner needs read access to one container for 24 hours without receiving the account key. What fits?

  • AThe primary access key shared with the partner and rotated after 24 hours
  • BA SAS token with read permission and a 24-hour expiry
  • CThe Owner role on the storage account for 24 hours
  • DA public container so that the partner can read it without a token
Show the answer

Answer: B. A SAS gives limited, time-bound access.

S3An issued SAS must be revocable without rotating account keys. What should have been used?

  • AAn account SAS
  • BThe primary key
  • CA tag
  • DA stored access policy
Show the answer

Answer: D. Deleting or editing the stored access policy revokes the SAS tokens that reference it.

S4Which SAS type is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials and is the most secure?

  • AAccount SAS
  • BUser delegation SAS
  • CService SAS
  • DThe access key
Show the answer

Answer: B. User delegation SAS avoids using the account key.

S5Why do accounts have two access keys?

  • AOne for reading and one for writing blobs and files
  • BOne for blobs and one for files in the account
  • CSo one can be rotated while applications use the other
  • DThey are identical backups that Azure keeps in two regions
Show the answer

Answer: C. Two keys allow rotation without downtime.

S6Domain users must access an Azure Files share with their own identities. What should be configured?

  • AThe account key shared with every user who needs access to the share
  • BA public container so that the share is readable by anyone
  • CIdentity-based authentication with RBAC roles on the share
  • DA budget that limits the transactions on the share
Show the answer

Answer: C. Identity-based access plus share-level roles uses user identities.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does a SAS token provide?

Show the answer

Limited, time-bound access without sharing the account key.

R2What is a stored access policy for?

Show the answer

Managing and revoking SAS tokens without regenerating keys.

R3How many access keys does an account have?

Show the answer

Two.

R4Which SAS type uses Entra credentials?

Show the answer

User delegation SAS.

R5What does a private endpoint give a storage account?

Show the answer

A private IP address in your virtual network.

R6Name one identity source for Azure Files.

Show the answer

For example on-premises AD DS, Microsoft Entra Domain Services or Entra Kerberos.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Network firewall rules, service endpoint, private endpoint, trusted services
SAS user delegation (Entra), service, account; permissions, expiry, IP, HTTPS
Stored access policy revoke or change service SAS without new keys; five per resource
Keys two keys, rotate, Key Vault, prefer Entra ID and RBAC
Azure Files identity AD DS, Entra Domain Services, Entra Kerberos + RBAC and NTFS
